disclosures.content_overlap: Content-word overlap here is the share of the reference's words outside the stop list found in the hypothesis, per clip. It is not the plan's sampled figures, whose definition was not recorded: read it only among this report's rows.
disclosures.cut: An ASLLVD real clip with its own annotated sign is cut there; every other clip, generated clips included, takes its entry's median position. Plan and stitching are the same.
disclosures.gpu: v1's stored forms state an NVIDIA L40S, and the job refuses another type. The stored A5 reports state none, though their hypotheses reproduced on an RTX 6000 Ada.
disclosures.humans: None of this shows human comprehension, and none of it is a claim about M1 or release.
disclosures.independence: The generator trained on these real clips, and they share a monocular MediaPipe path with its training data and with the parent's: an oracle reading high does not separate source from format as a two-view clip would.
disclosures.oracle_limits: Neither a low nor a high oracle separates format from source by itself: real word clips are MediaPipe monocular too. Live for a low oracle: selection by best of 16, d2 decoding, a different signer per word, a cut fitted on ASLLVD and applied to WLASL and RIT, fewer words with each core stretched, a source favouring generated clips.
disclosures.parsing: Shared helpers parse the whole mix, and v1_training_signs holds ids of the sentence set no job here names at merge, as earlier reads did. Nothing of either reaches an output.
disclosures.pick: The real clip is a chance pick, one per entry in a draw, by a hash of draw and entry: no instrument chose it. Each generated clip was its recogniser's best of 16.
disclosures.round_trip: d2's round trip smooths real motion; a real clip's untracked frames go in as the dataset serves them, with no fill.
disclosures.rule: A contrast is above or below only if its paired t interval over draws excludes zero on both margin over still and BLEU in the same direction; otherwise it is unresolved. The clip bootstrap interval decides nothing. Three mirror draws make unresolved likely there.
disclosures.seeds: Seeds are not independent replicates: a draw's seeds share its clips, words and plan. A two-word clip has one other order, the same under every seed. Moved rows take only clips whose word sequence changed.
disclosures.shuffle: Each word keeps its planned core frames and the gap lengths keep their places, so every word's rendered core is frame for frame the unshuffled form's. The joins are bridged anew.
disclosures.shuffle_drop: A large drop may also come from the rebuilt joins or the different still, which these rows do not fully separate. On a small drop, BLEU can see order-invariant signals such as length and pose, and a form with near-zero margin has nothing to lose.
disclosures.v1: v1 is read only here, never for a loss, a rerank or a best-of-N, on A5's top10 on D20: a different arm and different clips from the official score, which this does not decompose. It trained on 234 of D20's clips and selected on 265 more, so by_clip_subset rows matter. Its forms are the stored composed states of this job's first read, each held to its hash. Stored A5 reports hold no still and no mismatched NLL, so composition, still and blank are read again and checked against them. Six of its seven anchors and the canary are checked; still_monocular has no stored v1 read.
disclosures.words_lacked: The oracle lacks the seven added entries, which have no real clip in the three corpora and no clip of the same spelling taken from elsewhere, Sem-Lex-only words and words not served, and R is reshared among those left. Oracle against composition therefore mixes real clips with the words the oracle lacks and the frames they free: oracle against covered is the same words.

note: report only: no rule, bar or verdict here gates anything
reading: This reads A5's top10 on D20, mean 2.402, a different arm and different clips from the held-out set's official 2.400 (arm W14b with gains, best of 16, real 4.033). It does not decompose M1, and nothing here can be carried over to that set. A D20 result suggests how much word order this arm's reading on these clips holds through this instrument, and so whether the question is worth asking of the official arm; it does not say what share of the official score is word order. The same rule: above or below only if the t interval over draws excludes zero on both margin over still and BLEU in the same direction; otherwise unresolved; the clip interval decides nothing. Whether a drop exists is decided by paired.moved.shuffled_minus_composition by that rule. Below: a drop exists. Above: shuffling raises the reading. Unresolved is not small: this read cannot say whether shuffling moves the reading. How large is read on v1_gap.share_of_composition_gap_removed_by_shuffling, with the parent's 50% and the mirror's 39% beside it and no cut: a drop with the share's t interval around them holds about as much as theirs, below them less and still some, above them more. Neither a large nor a small share is the better outcome. BLEU is n-grams, so a reader that gets every word right, in the input's order, loses BLEU mechanically: paired.content_word_overlap falling too points to more than n-gram order. A drop may also come from the rebuilt joins or the different still, which these rows do not fully separate, and a read of English order is no evidence that a person follows it or that it is signing. v1 trained on 234 of D20's clips and selected on 265 more, so its memory could drive a drop: v1_gap.by_clip_subset gives the clean 178. v1 is read only, never for a loss, a rerank or a best-of-N. No target moves, M1 stays read on the held-out set and nothing here touches that set. None of it shows human comprehension.
